sources.note: Direct page quotes Ancient Cities of the Indus Valley Civilization (1998),p60. Toilet identification and regular labor arrangements interpreted; no universal household claim, invention claim or caste attribution.

sources.note: Direct original1921ASI report excerpt,p13,objectsA168,A292,A233,photograph2749. Modern Kenoyer2021commentary identifies varied cart types. Excavation year is not ancient manufacture date.

sources.title: Harappa Archaeological Research Project: Textile impressions
sources.note: Direct HARP caption: toy bed, Harappan phase2600 to 1900BCE, tightly woven normal weave and uniformly spun thread impressions. No unsupported cotton identification.

sources.title: Suryanarayan and colleagues: Lipid residues in pottery from the Indus Civilisation
sources.note: Original JAS125(2021)105291,DOI10.1016/j.jas.2020.105291. Full indexed publisher abstract/highlights and institutional repository checked; PMC direct CAPTCHA. Milk/meat, ambiguous mixtures, urban/rural similarities and continuity; not a quantified diet or reliable species breakdown.

sources.title: Jonathan Mark Kenoyer: Stone beads, methods of study
sources.note: Direct original2017scholarlyPDF,printed160/PDFpage10,SurfaceDocumentation: Chanhudaro rough pecked and elaborate Ernestite-drilled beads in same workshop; absence of string wear. No price claim.

sources.title: Jonathan Mark Kenoyer: Cubical weights
sources.note: Direct research-site object caption, weights from Allahdino/Harappa;ratios1:2:4:8:16:32 and13.7gcommonweight. Taxation is only possible, not asserted.

sources.title: Robbins Schug and colleagues: Infection, disease and biosocial processes at the end of the Indus civilization
sources.note: Direct original PLOS2013fulltext,Materials/Methods,Results and Discussion. Fragmentary skeletons, lesions consistent with infections, differential burial populations. Do not call160 the analyzed disease sample:45laterburials omitted from focal comparison.
